newsitem.title: USA: Gillette buying Duracell for $7 billion.
newsitem.headline: Gillette buying Duracell for $7 billion.

text.p: Gillette Co., the shaving products powerhouse, made a big leap into the wider consumer products market Thursday, announcing that it was acquiring battery maker Duracell International Inc. for about $7 billion in stock.
Bear Stearns & Co. analyst Constance Maneaty said the deal was "a perfect fit."

Gillette said it will issue about 108 million shares in the stock transaction, putting the value at about $7 billion. Duracell stockholders will received 0.904 share of Gillette for each Duracell share they own.
Trading in both issues was halted on the New York Stock Exchange immediately after the announcement, which had been reported earlier by the Wall Street Journal and other media, including Reuters.
Duracell's stock shot up $7.125 to $55.50 in advance of the announcement while Gillette fell $1.25 to $63.75. The
transaction, which still needs the approval of stockholders of both companies, is intended to be a tax-free exchange of shares, the companies said.
The announcement said that Kohlberg Kravis & Roberts Co., L.P., which owns about 34 percent of Duracell's outstanding shares, agreed to vote in favour of the merger.

"It's a very good deal," said Goldman Sachs analyst Amy Low. "It meets every criteria ... including a global brand with a No. 1 position, room for international expansion, high margins and significant synergies, particularly in the distribution and sales force."
Gillette Chairman Alfred Zeien said he expected the deal to add to the company's earnings immediately.

"Duracell is already the world leader in the highly profitable and fast-growing alkaline battery market, and has the potential to grow that share in association with the Gillette worldwide marketing and distribution organisation," he said in a statement.
Founded in 1901, Gillette is the world leader in male grooming products, a category that includes razors and blades, shaving preparations and electric shavers.
It is also the world's top seller of toothbrushes and oral care appliances with its Oral-B line. It also makes Parker pens and Braun shavers and other appliances.
Duracell International is the world's leading manufacturer of alkaline batteries.It also markets rechargeable battery packs, primary lithium batteries and zinc air batteries.
